network_features.description: Connected network graph for indoor routing with Dijkstra's algorithm. Nodes are IfcSpace rooms, doors and stairs; edges are door, corridor and stair connections. Coordinates are in metres.

export_format:
Extracted by extract_ifc_data.py and loaded by load_database.py. The schema maps IFC entities to database tables as follows:

- IfcSpace -> rooms table (id, name, floor, type, area, center_x, center_y, center_z)
- IfcDoor -> doors table (id, name, floor, width, height, material, status)
- IfcWindow -> windows table (id, name, floor, width, height, material, status)
- IfcBuildingStorey -> floors table (id, name, level, area)
- Routing nodes/edges -> network_nodes and network_edges tables

CSV files provided:
- src/data/bim/rooms.csv (105 rooms, 3 floors)
- src/data/bim/doors.csv (153 doors)
- src/data/bim/windows.csv (191 windows)
- src/data/bim/floors.csv (3 floors)
- src/data/routing/network_graph.json (264 nodes, 502 edges)
extraction_method: Uses ifcopenshell to read IfcSpace rooms directly (room Name + LongName type), resolves the storey through IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure, computes floor area from the space's bottom triangles, and takes room/door/stair centres from world-coordinate geometry in metres. Doors and windows use OverallWidth/OverallHeight converted from project units to metres. The routing graph is fully connected across all three floors, with stair links and a fallback vertical link where the IFC has no stair on a floor.
